title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: All directors and employees
tiers.description: All directors and employees of SKYCITY. Subject to the fundamental insider trading prohibition at all times; 'trade' is defined as buying or selling securities (excluding gift or inheritance).

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: All directors of SKYCITY and relevant subsidiaries; the CEO, his/her direct reports and their direct reports; staff involved in compiling or accessing financial performance reports for significant business components; and any other employee or associate designated in writing by the company. Subject to the Additional Trading Restrictions and Approved Trading Procedure (window periods and prior written consent).

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Spouse or partner, close relative (including dependent child), or a company or trust in which the person has a material interest or can influence trustee decisions; the fundamental rule applies even where securities are held in such a name.

definitions.hedging_definition: transactions or arrangements ... which operate to limit the economic risk of a Restricted Person's interest in SKYCITY securities

windows.start_anchor: day after announcement to NZX/ASX of the most recently completed full year (30 June) or half year (31 December) results, whichever occurred last
windows.end_anchor: 60 days after that announcement, or such other date as the board may specify

rules.detail: The Approved Trading Procedure expressly extends beyond sale/purchase to transactions or arrangements with a substantially similar economic effect, which catches an OTC put/call; prior written consent via the Request for Consent form is required, tradeable only within 10 trading days of consent and only within the window period unless waived.
rules.evidence: entering into transactions or arrangements which have a substantially similar economic effect as the sale or purchase of a SKYCITY security, or which operate to limit the economic risk of a Restricted Person's interest in SKYCITY securities

rules.detail: For staff who are not Restricted Persons, only the fundamental insider-trading prohibition applies, and 'trade' is defined narrowly as buying or selling securities; derivatives are not named or otherwise swept in for this tier.
rules.evidence: 'trade' includes buying or selling securities, except where the acquisition or disposal occurs by way of gift or inheritance.

rules.detail: Whether a proposed arrangement would limit the economic risk of entitlements that have not vested is an express criterion the Company Secretary/board weighs (in its absolute discretion) when deciding whether to consent; there is no outright statutory bar, but this counts against approval.
rules.evidence: whether the sale or purchase, or transactions or arrangements, would have the effect of limiting the economic risk of the Restricted Person's entitlement to SKYCITY securities that have not vested

rules.detail: Hedging of vested holdings requires prior written consent as an 'economic risk limiting' arrangement; the policy does not separately distinguish a vested-but-holding-locked state.
rules.evidence: which operate to limit the economic risk of a Restricted Person's interest in SKYCITY securities

rules.detail: Hedging is only named in the Approved Trading Procedure, which applies to Restricted Persons only.
Monetisation is not named, but a prepaid forward or similar arrangement with an economic effect substantially similar to a sale falls within the Procedure's scope and requires prior written consent.
rules.evidence: transactions or arrangements which have a substantially similar economic effect as the sale or purchase of a SKYCITY security

rules.detail: No mechanism outside the Restricted Persons procedure sweeps in monetisation transactions.
Short selling is not named anywhere in the Policy.
Securities lending is not named anywhere in the Policy.
CFDs are not named but would be an arrangement with an economic effect substantially similar to sale/purchase, requiring prior written consent for Restricted Persons.
rules.evidence: transactions or arrangements which have a substantially similar economic effect as the sale or purchase of a SKYCITY security

rules.detail: Margin lending is never prohibited or named as requiring consent to enter into; the only reference is that a secured lender's forced sale (e.g. under a margin lending arrangement) is excluded from the Additional Restrictions, which presupposes margin lending arrangements are a contemplated, permitted practice.
rules.evidence: a disposal of SKYCITY securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement

rules.detail: Granting security, a charge, lien or pledge over SKYCITY securities is not named and is not caught by the 'trade' or Approved Trading Procedure wording, which focus on sale/purchase or economic-risk-limiting arrangements rather than encumbrance itself.

The Policy addresses only the consequence of a secured lender's forced sale (excluded from the Additional Restrictions); it does not otherwise regulate, permit-with-conditions, or prohibit secured financing arrangements generally.
Framed as guidance ('should be avoided') rather than an absolute 'must not' bar, and no clearance, waiver or carve-out mechanism is tied to it.
rules.evidence: As a general rule, short-term trading of shares (within a six month period) should be avoided.

clearance.approver: Company Secretary, the board, or another officer appointed by and acting on behalf of the board (or, in the Company Secretary's absence, a person the Company Secretary authorises)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: 5 business days after the purchase or sale
clearance.section: Approved Trading Procedure; Declarations of Security Holdings
clearance.evidence: A 'Request for Consent to Trade in Listed Securities' (Attachment 1 to this Policy) must be submitted to and approved by the Company Secretary prior to any trade ... Restricted Persons must file with the company a new declaration of security holding within 5 business days of the purchase or sale of any SKYCITY securities.
The Additional Restrictions do not apply to staff who are not designated as Restricted Persons.

short_term.evidence: As a general rule, short-term trading of shares (within a six month period) should be avoided.

exceptions.evidence: Exceptional circumstances for these purposes include severe financial hardship, compulsion by court order or any other circumstance that is deemed exceptional by the board.
any other circumstance that is deemed exceptional by the board

acquisition of SKYCITY securities through a dividend reinvestment plan; acquisition of SKYCITY securities through a share purchase plan available to all retail shareholders; acquisition of SKYCITY securities through a rights issue
the disposal of SKYCITY securities through the acceptance of a takeover offer
dealings that do not result in a change to the beneficial interest in SKYCITY securities
a disposal of SKYCITY securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
participation in an employee share plan operated by SKYCITY (e.g. applying for an allocation of SKYCITY securities under an employee share offer)

exemption_authority: The board may waive the Additional Restrictions for a Restricted Person in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship, compulsion by court order, or other board-determined exceptional circumstance), on application to the Company Secretary with supporting evidence; any waiver runs for 10 trading days. The board may also approve updates, amendments to and exemptions from the Policy generally.
jurisdiction_overlays: Securities Markets (Disclosure of Relevant Interests by Directors and Officers) Regulations 2003 (NZ)

bespoke_clauses.clause: transactions or arrangements which have a substantially similar economic effect as the sale or purchase of a SKYCITY security, or which operate to limit the economic risk of a Restricted Person's interest in SKYCITY securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An OTC collar (purchased put and written call) over vested shares is squarely caught for a Restricted Person and needs prior written consent, executed within 10 trading days of consent and only within the open trading window unless a hardship waiver is obtained.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of SKYCITY securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale of collared shares under the loan is expressly excluded from the window-period and consent regime, so lender enforcement is not blocked by the Policy even during a closed period.

bespoke_clauses.clause: whether the sale or purchase, or transactions or arrangements, would have the effect of limiting the economic risk of the Restricted Person's entitlement to SKYCITY securities that have not vested
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Hedging or collaring unvested equity is an express factor weighed against consent, so a funded collar is realistically available only once the underlying shares have vested.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Additional Restrictions do not apply to staff who are not designated as Restricted Persons.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the bank's counterparty director or executive is not a Restricted Person, no consent, window or approval regime under this Policy constrains entry into a collar or its secured loan at all, subject only to the general insider trading prohibition.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy covers certain provisions and procedures that apply to SKYCITY directors and employees but does not constitute an exhaustive set of statements about the law.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: No express prohibition on margin lending, other secured financing or granting security over SKYCITY securities exists anywhere in the Policy, so the loan leg of a funded collar is not itself barred by this document.

summary: A funded OTC collar over vested shares is workable for a SKYCITY Restricted Person, but only through the Approved Trading Procedure: because the put/call structure 'operates to limit the economic risk' of the holding, it requires prior written consent from the Company Secretary (or the board), must be entered within the open 60-day post-results trading window (or under a hardship/court-order waiver), and must be executed within 10 trading days of consent or the consent lapses. The Policy is silent on margin lending, other secured financing and encumbrance generally, and expressly excludes a secured lender's enforcement sale from the Additional Restrictions, so the loan leg secured on the collared shares is not itself prohibited, though collaring shares that remain unvested is a factor likely to count against consent. Directors and employees who are not Restricted Persons face no consent regime at all beyond the fundamental insider-trading prohibition, so a collar for that population is essentially unconstrained by this Policy provided no inside information is held. Restricted Persons must also lodge a new security-holding declaration within 5 business days of any trade, and officers carry separate NZX/ASX disclosure obligations. Overall verdict: permitted with prior written consent (or a board waiver) for vested holdings, with no policy-level bar on the secured loan itself.
